confirmed: The local PDF is arXiv:2601.12740v1 [cs.HC], dated 19 Jan 2026, with 35 pages; its title and author list match the form (p. 1 and PDF page count). The entire markdown conversion, including Appendix I, was read.

The comparative study is a lab experiment with randomized within-person tool order: every participant used TreeWriter and Google Docs + Gemini, with assignment to four order/content groups. lab_rct, within_person_order, and ai_design are supported (p. 14, Section 5.2; p. 27, Appendix D and Table 6).

The reported comparative cohort contains 12 students; Figure 9 shows response counts totaling 12 for each tool and item. These are repeated responses from the same people, not separate people per arm, texts, or independent ratings; the analyzed cohort is below 50 (p. 13, Section 5.1; p. 17, Figure 9; p. 25, Table 4).

The form correctly preserves the source discrepancy in education: Section 5.1 says five undergraduate, three master?s, and four PhD students, while Table 4 lists five undergraduates, three master?s students, three PhD students, and one JD student. Two women, ten men, prior AI co-writing experience, and $50 CAD compensation are stated in Section 5.1 (p. 13; p. 25, Table 4).

Task sizes and timing match: a 4,000-word article with six editing subtasks, an 800-word essay, 20 minutes per task per tool, and approximately 2.5 hours per session. The essay topics concern university teaching and students? mental health (pp. 13-14, Sections 5.1-5.2; p. 27, Figure 10; p. 29, Appendix F).
TreeWriter uses GPT-5 for its writing assistant and GPT-4.1 for its editing buttons; the comparative baseline is Google Docs with Gemini (p. 13, Section 4.7; p. 14, Section 5.3).

The recorded measures concern perceived tool support: post-task items use a 7-point Likert scale and CSI items use a 1-10 scale. CSI was completed after the creative-writing task. No creativity or diversity score of the essays or edits is reported (p. 14, Section 5.4; pp. 26-27, Appendix C; p. 31, Figure 11; p. 32, Figure 12).

All three reported q-values and multiplicity labels match: Explore Ideas q = 0.01, Creativity q = 0.033, and Track Ideas q = 0.033, from Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with within-category Benjamini-Hochberg correction; creative-writing post-task m = 5 and CSI m = 10 (p. 16, Figure 8; p. 30, Appendix G).
The creativity response bands match the PDF figure: Google Docs 1-2 N=2, 3-4 N=4, 5-6 N=3, 9-10 N=3; TreeWriter 3-4 N=1, 5-6 N=3, 7-8 N=2, 9-10 N=6 (p. 17, Figure 9, Creativity row and color legend).

The idea-tracking response bands match the PDF figure: Google Docs 1-2 N=1, 3-4 N=4, 5-6 N=1, 7-8 N=5, 9-10 N=1; TreeWriter 5-6 N=2, 7-8 N=4, 9-10 N=6 (p. 17, Figure 9, Track Ideas row and color legend).

The one-line finding accurately describes higher self-reported idea exploration, creativity support, and idea tracking with the three printed q-values; it does not claim higher scored writing creativity (p. 16, Figure 8; p. 17, Figure 9; p. 30, Appendix G).

The six-person formative study and eight-person field deployment also report questionnaire/interview evidence rather than scored creative output; the deployment has no comparison arm, and the samples do not overlap (p. 5, Section 3.1; p. 18, Section 6; p. 25, Appendix A; pp. 32-33, Appendix H).

Core = no, context_class = none, and failure of the sample-size and output-scoring criteria are supported. Although tool order was randomized, no study combines random assignment of AI assistance with creativity/diversity scored on human output; therefore has_randomized_people_study is false under this checker?s definition (pp. 13-14, Sections 5.1-5.4; p. 27, Appendix D; pp. 30-33, Appendices G-H).
This is an original system evaluation, not a synthesis; the empty synthesis fields and absence of pooled estimates are appropriate (p. 5, Section 3; p. 13, Section 5; p. 18, Section 6).
summary: The 12-person randomized-order study measured self-reported tool support, with no creativity or diversity scored on writing. Reported results match the PDF, but five corrections are needed for randomization-count provenance, missing studies, appendix coverage, company involvement, and code availability.
